# ns3-ntn-toolkit

> ns3-ntn-toolkit is an open-source ns-3.43 simulation platform for 5G and 6G
> non-terrestrial networks (NTN). It carries fourteen custom modules and three
> vendored upstream stacks in one tree, so that a LEO satellite's SGP4 position
> drives a real 5G NR spectrum PHY, a handover decision rides a real Xn interface
> with a real propagation delay, and every reported KPI came off a packet that
> crossed the air interface. Its distinguishing property is that the decision
> plane and the measurement plane are the same plane.

Author: Muhammad Uzair, Independent Researcher, ORCID 0009-0002-4104-2680.
License: GPL-2.0-only. Built on ns-3.43.

## What it is, in one line

An ns-3 based LEO, MEO and GEO satellite plus 5G NR-NTN plus O-RAN network
simulator for researchers building 6G non-terrestrial networks.

## Who it is for

Researchers and engineers working on non-terrestrial networks, LEO satellite
constellations, 5G and 6G NR-NTN, satellite O-RAN and RIC placement, conditional
handover and mobility management, mega-constellation scale simulation,
terahertz and sub-terahertz links, space-air-ground integrated networks,
V2X over satellite, network slicing, and reinforcement learning for satellite
radio resource management.

## Key capabilities

- SGP4 and SDP4 orbital propagation of real Starlink, OneWeb, Kuiper and
  Iridium NEXT two-line elements, plus Walker-Delta and Walker-Star generators,
  contact-graph routing over inter-satellite links with limb clearance.
- A real 5G NR data plane under satellite mobility: SpectrumPhy, LDPC error
  model, HARQ with an NTN-stretched process pool, RLC, PDCP, RRC, EPC and GTP,
  on either the mmWave FR2 backend or 5G-LENA nr at FR1.
- 3GPP TR 38.811 and TR 38.821 NTN channel modeling and link budget, calibrated
  against the Set-1 LEO-600 reference parameters with separate offset and
  elevation-slope gates.
- Conditional handover for LEO with time-to-exit estimation from real orbit
  propagation, and the standardized trigger set: TS 38.331 CondEvent A3, D1 on a
  fixed reference location, T1 on its absolute broadcast epoch, Rel-18 D2 on a
  moving ephemeris reference, plus elevation and timing-advance mechanisms.
- NR-NTN control plane: SIB19 with cellSpecificKoffset consumed by the
  scheduler, timing advance that differs between transparent and regenerative
  payloads because the feeder leg is in the geometry, and DRX that gates a flow.
- Space O-RAN: E2AP termination, E2SM-KPM under TS 28.552 names, E2SM-RC control
  actions that actuate a real handover, A1 policy distribution, three RIC
  placements (on-board real-time, gateway, cloud) whose E2 latency comes from
  live slant geometry, Release 19 regenerative payload options, the WG3 conflict
  taxonomy, and a FlexRIC bridge for the wire-level path. The in-simulation E2
  transport is an ns-3 header with toolkit-internal type values, not ASN.1 APER
  over SCTP.
- Sub-terahertz and terahertz physics from 100 GHz to 1 THz on the ITU-R
  recommendations: P.676-13 line-by-line gaseous absorption over a layered
  atmosphere, P.618-13 tropospheric scintillation, P.838-3 rain, P.840 cloud and
  fog, Tatarskii turbulence, pointing error, ultra-massive MIMO, RIS and ISAC.
- NVIDIA Sionna RT GPU ray tracing over a socket, with provenance on every query
  so a run states whether it was ray traced or fell back to free space.
- Space-air-ground integrated networking with ground, UAV, HAPS and LEO layers,
  a TR 36.777 air-to-ground channel that declares its 300 m validated-height
  boundary, and store-and-forward across contact gaps.
- Network slicing with eMBB, URLLC and mMTC over per-5QI dedicated bearers and
  SLA percentiles taken from a delay histogram rather than a mean.
- Satellite-assisted V2X with NR sidelink PC5 Mode 2 and SAE J2735 basic safety
  messages encoded per the standard, including its UPER offset-from-lower-bound
  integers.
- SCF-222 FAPI MAC-PHY adapter on a live NR service access point.
- Observability: one scene recorder feeding NetSimulyzer, Cesium CZML, InfluxDB
  line protocol and Grafana, with link topology and a documented time anchor.
- A FastAPI network digital twin that predicts handovers from live ephemeris and
  actuates them back into a running simulation, sharing one guard with the
  exporter.
- Gymnasium 1.0 environments for handover selection, beam management, slice
  admission and power control, over a shared-memory bridge with a versioned
  schema. The bundled trainers are single-agent PPO and SAC over N independent
  environment copies, not MAPPO or MASAC.

## Measured results carried in the repository

- Conditional handover, ten seeds on a 780 km shell: a time-to-exit-aware policy
  reaches 83.14 percent handover success on 134.6 handovers per run with zero
  ping-pong, against an A3 RSRP baseline at 463.3 handovers, 69.16 percent
  success and a 50.23 percent ping-pong rate. A location-based policy reaches
  98.69 percent success at 57.07 percent ping-pong.
- O-RAN xApp routing: 7,738 near-real-time decisions producing 71,967 actuated
  actions across five active xApps, with the control loop measured end to end.

## How claims are kept checkable

- Every scenario writes sim_health.csv labelling each KPI measured, modeled or
  configured, so a number derived from an equation cannot be printed as if it
  came from a packet.
- tools/check_ntn_standards.py runs sixteen gates covering the TR 38.821 link
  budget, orbital geometry, the published latency bands and all five NTN
  handover trigger classes.
- tools/check_doc_claims.py fails when a document makes a capability claim the
  code contradicts or quotes a number the committed data does not carry.
- SCOPE_AND_LIMITATIONS.md is the authoritative statement of what the toolkit
  does not model, including the absence of Release 19 AI/ML lifecycle
  management and the multi-tap NTN-TDL.
